log: |rule|Species Clause: Limit one of each Pokémon

decisions.thought: Opponent has three Steel-types plus Incineroar, making Ground coverage extremely dominant. Mega Garchomp has immense offensive pressure, Scarf Gholdengo offers fast revenge killing, and Dragonite provides a reliable win condition with Multiscale.

Incineroar leads for Intimidate and Fake Out, which blunts the physical attackers like Garchomp and Dragonite. Garchomp gives a fast Mega-capable threat, and Gholdengo's special power covers Primarina and Volcarona. This trio gives the best coverage across their six.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Looking at team preview against their dragonite, gholdengo, mimikyu, garchomp, volcarona, primarina lineup, I'm weighing my own options: incineroar for intimidate and fake out utility against their physical threats, garchomp with mega potential for speed, plus gholdengo, kingambit, sinistcha, and archaludon as backup picks. I'm leaning toward incineroar and garchomp as strong leads, though I need to reconsider garchomp's ground-type moves since gholdengo's steel typing blocks that coverage.

Fairy resists Dark so that's neutral, fine either way. I'll settle on Incineroar, Garchomp, and Gholdengo as my team, with Gholdengo's Steel typing hitting Primarina's Fairy side hard via Make It Rain, and lead with Incineroar.

decisions.thought: Fake Out is usable on turn 1 and Incineroar is slower than Garchomp, so the flinch stops a Garchomp attack this turn. It also chips a little damage while setting up Flare Blitz next turn.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: The opponent's Garchomp might be holding Garchompite. Since it's turn 1 with both leads just sent out, Fake Out works on Incineroar and will flinch Garchomp while dealing minor damage, setting up for a Flare Blitz next turn — though Garchomp's base 102 Speed outpaces Incineroar's 60.

decisions.thought: Garchomp naturally outspeeds Incineroar. Mega Evolving reduces Speed slightly, but Garchomp-Mega is still faster than base 60 Incineroar while massively boosting Attack to offset the Intimidate drop and deal heavy STAB super-effective damage with Earthquake.
Mega Garchomp naturally outspeeds Incineroar. Even at -1 Attack, STAB Earthquake deals massive super-effective damage to Incineroar or severely dents anything switching in.

Flare Blitz is resisted by Garchomp's Dragon typing, so attacking is poor. Parting Shot drops its Attack again before I pivot out, which weakens its Earthquake and Outrage threats. That keeps my Garchomp and Gholdengo healthier for the switch.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking Garchomp's typing against Flare Blitz - Fire hits neutrally since Dragon/Ground doesn't resist it, so Incineroar's attack should do normal damage there.

Now I'm weighing Protect versus Parting Shot to further cripple Garchomp's Attack while pivoting to Gholdengo, considering how Gholdengo's Steel/Ghost typing and moves like Shadow Ball or Make It Rain matchup against Garchomp's Earthquake and Outrage.

I'll go with Parting Shot — it weakens Incineroar's offense further while letting me pivot to a better-positioned attacker.

decisions.thought: Incineroar is at 90/202 and threatened by a super-effective Earthquake, and the only legal actions are switches. Gholdengo would take a 2x Ground hit, while our Garchomp is neutral to Ground and faster than their weakened Garchomp, so it can hit back hard.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
My Incineroar is at 90/202 against Garchomp, who's at 88% HP with lowered attack and special attack from stat drops, after taking a big earthquake hit. I'm weighing whether to switch to my own Garchomp, potentially mega evolving for a speed boost, or bring in Gholdengo instead, while noting the opponent's Garchomp has Sand Force and possibly carries its mega stone.

Garchomp takes a reduced EQ fine with Rough Skin chip in return, while Gholdengo would be terrible to switch in since Steel is weak to Ground. Protect isn't available since this is a forced switch decision, so Garchomp is the right call here.

decisions.thought: Our Garchomp is likely faster, and Outrage is super effective against the opposing Dragon/Ground Garchomp. Its Attack is at -2, so it can't threaten us much first. Outrage should knock it out, so I'm saving Mega Evolution.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm our Garchomp facing the opposing Garchomp, which is down to 88% HP with -2 attack and -1 special attack, weakening its Earthquake and sand-boosted moves. I'm comparing our speed stats to figure out who moves first this turn.

Outrage looks like the strongest option—Dragon-type STAB that hits super effectively against their Dragon/Ground typing, and mega evolving gives us Sand Force for extra power. I'm estimating the damage from mega Garchomp's Outrage against their defense stat to see if it can knock them out given their reduced HP.

I'm trying to figure out whether the current attack stats already reflect Mega Garchomp or not, since its base stats differ from regular Garchomp. Given the ambiguity, I'll just go with using Outrage without Mega evolving to keep things simple, since Mega's benefits here seem marginal anyway.

decisions.thought: Mega Garchomp is slower than base Garchomp and sitting at -2 Attack, making it vulnerable to an immediate Dragon STAB knockout. Switching to Dragonite with Multiscale easily sponges any incoming attack.
Only one legal action is available: Outrage. It is super effective against Dragonite at 34% HP and Garchomp is faster, so it should knock out before Dragonite moves.
Opposing Garchomp is locked into Outrage and outspeeds Dragonite, which will faint this turn. Switching to Gholdengo resists Outrage completely and takes minimal damage.
Only one legal action is available: Outrage. It is the only move offered this turn, so it is the correct choice regardless of matchup.
Opposing Garchomp is locked into Outrage, which Gholdengo resists. With Choice Scarf, Gholdengo outspeeds Garchomp and deals massive STAB damage with Make It Rain.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
**Analyzing the Options**

I've determined that Gholdengo's Choice Scarf, Make It Rain, will easily knock out Garchomp, even with the SpA drop and Garchomp's Outrage lock. The math confirms Make It Rain is the play here.


**Deciding the Next Move**

I'm now calculating if switching Gholdengo into Heatran to handle a potential switch is better. Evaluating different scenarios like Heatran's Lava Plume and the potential for a subsequent Gholdengo switch to be a winning play, will determine the next course of action.

Raw answer:

decisions.thought: Garchomp outspeeds Gholdengo (169 vs 84 base Speed), and Gholdengo is at about 30% HP. Earthquake is 2x super effective against Steel and cannot be blocked by Good as Gold, so it should knock Gholdengo out before it moves. Mega isn't needed for this KO.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
My Garchomp can mega evolve and still has decent HP left, while Gholdengo is down to 30% but its ability blocks status moves. Since Gholdengo is Steel/Ghost, Earthquake hits it super effectively, and Garchomp outspeeds it easily, so this looks like a strong finishing move.

Running the numbers, Earthquake with Garchomp's attack and STAB should easily knock out Gholdengo's remaining health, so mega evolving isn't even necessary here—it'd be overkill. I'm also checking whether Gholdengo's Make It Rain could threaten Garchomp back, but with its special attack lowered, the damage shouldn't be too severe.

decisions.thought: Garchomp has fainted, so I must switch. Gholdengo is at full HP and the opposing Gholdengo is at 30%, so one super-effective hit (Shadow Ball or Thunderbolt) should KO it. Make It Rain can't knock out a full-HP Gholdengo, so this is the safer choice.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Garchomp down, I'm weighing my remaining options: a full-health Gholdengo with Life Orb versus a heavily damaged Incineroar. Against the opponent's weakened Gholdengo, I'm considering whether to go with Make It Rain, Shadow Ball, or Thunderbolt given the Steel/Ghost matchup.

Flare Blitz is 2x on Steel too, so Incineroar could also threaten Gholdengo, though it takes neutral damage back from Make It Rain. Speed-wise, Incineroar at base 80 is likely slower than the opposing Gholdengo, but since both Gholdengos share base 84 speed, ours at 136 should match or tie with theirs.

Still, Gholdengo is my strongest pick here at full HP with Life Orb -- Shadow Ball or Thunderbolt should secure the KO, and even if I go second, Make It Rain won't break through 164 HP at full health. I'll go with Gholdengo.

decisions.thought: Our Gholdengo is locked into Make It Rain at -4 Special Attack and will easily be knocked out by opposing Gholdengo's Shadow Ball. Garchomp has high HP and cleanly threatens both remaining opponents with Ground STAB. Switching to Garchomp is the safest play.
Our Gholdengo is much faster (136 vs 84) and the opponent's is at 30% HP with -4 SpA. Thunderbolt is super effective against Steel/Ghost, so it should knock out before the opponent moves.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Our Gholdengo at 164 HP with Life Orb is faster than the opponent's weakened Gholdengo, whose SpA is already down four stages from repeated Make It Rain use, leaving it sitting at roughly 30% health. That makes another Make It Rain from our side a near-guaranteed knockout given the speed advantage.

decisions.thought: Earthquake is super effective against Gholdengo and will easily OHKO it, while also covering a potential switch to Incineroar.

Our Gholdengo outspeeds Mega Garchomp (136 vs 92), and Garchomp is the only thing threatening our Gholdengo with Earthquake. Shadow Ball with STAB and Life Orb should knock out the ~95 HP Garchomp even at minimum roll, without Make It Rain's self-drop to our SpA.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking type matchups against Mega Garchomp: Thunderbolt is useless since it's part Ground, and Steel-type Make It Rain is neutral against its Dragon/Ground typing, so I'm weighing which move still gets through its defenses.

I'm estimating Make It Rain's damage with STAB and Life Orb against Garchomp's special defense, landing roughly in the 155-181 range per hit, which should be enough to pressure its remaining HP.

Checking Shadow Ball as an alternative, with STAB it still deals around 103-121 damage, enough to also take Garchomp down given its ~95 HP. Since Gholdengo outspeeds Garchomp and Shadow Ball doesn't carry the self-drop that Make It Rain has, Shadow Ball looks like the cleaner, more reliable kill.

decisions.thought: Only one legal action: switch to Incineroar. It's the only Pokémon left on my bench that can act, so I have to send it in against Mega Garchomp.
Incineroar is at 44% HP and weak to Ground. Even at -1 Attack, STAB Earthquake easily finishes it off and wins the match.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking the damage math: Incineroar at roughly 90/202 HP facing Mega Garchomp's Earthquake, factoring in Garchomp's attack drop and Incineroar's defensive typing where Ground hits neutrally against Fire/Dark.

Wait, actually Ground is super effective against Fire, so Earthquake likely nearly OHKOs Incineroar given Garchomp's speed advantage. Fake Out won't work since Incineroar's already been in play, Flare Blitz is weak against Dragon/Ground typing, and Parting Shot would further cripple Garchomp's attack but there's nothing left on the bench to switch into.

Parting Shot wouldn't accomplish much here since nothing changes. Protecting this turn to dodge the Earthquake seems safer, though I need to check if Flare Blitz could meaningfully dent mega Garchomp's health given its massive HP pool.

Running the numbers roughly, Incineroar's Flare Blitz only lands around 30% on Garchomp due to the resistance, not a KO. Meanwhile Garchomp's Earthquake one-shots Incineroar easily, so Protect just delays the inevitable unless I can outspeed or switch out safely.

Since we're losing this Pokémon regardless, I'm leaning toward Flare Blitz for the extra chip damage against Garchomp before it falls, factoring in that even with -2 Atk from Parting Shot, Garchomp's EQ still kills. Protect might buy a scouting turn but doesn't change the outcome against the remaining threats of Gholdengo and Dragonite.

Incineroar sits at 90/202 HP while the opposing Mega Garchomp is at 75%. Checking type matchups, Earthquake hits Incineroar neutrally since Fire/Dark has no Ground immunity or resistance.

Flare Blitz is resisted by Garchomp's Dragon typing, so it won't be enough to knock out the Mega even weakened. Parting Shot is tricky here since my bench appears empty—Incineroar might be my last mon standing, which would make the switch portion of that move unusable or forced to fail, so Protect might be safer given Garchomp's attack is already lowered.

Estimating Garchomp Mega's HP at roughly 200+, with 75% remaining putting it around 160, so Flare Blitz's ~129 damage would still leave it standing but significantly weakened.

Since Garchomp outspeeds Incineroar (92 vs 80), it moves first, and Earthquake likely KOs Incineroar outright if it's at 90 HP, which changes the calculus entirely -- Protect becomes less useful if Garchomp can simply kill Incineroar before it attacks.
